Three genes only; the rub cluster has no NovK/CloK/CouK homologue. PMID 18080113: "RubC3 is similar to NovJ, which, together with NovK, has been loosely implicated in the conversion of hydroxytyrosine to keto-tyrosine, although no NovK homologue was detected in the rub gene cluster"; no NovC homologue either, and the authors note some 4-hydroxyaminocoumarin genes "have yet to be discovered". NovJ/NovK are two subunits of one oxidase (Pacholec 2005, PMID 16171396), so this is a missing subunit rather than a missing step. rubC1 is a fusion of the NovL amide-synthetase and NovH tyrosine-adenylation domains in a single 1317-aa ORF (PMID 18080113), so the cassette does not map 1:1 onto novHIJK. It is retained despite carrying the NovL exit function (amide bond formation to the aminocoumarin amino group, excluded as novL/cloL/couL are in the other BB0007 rows), because the same ORF performs the NovH loading step.

The 3-hydroxyl of 4-MHA requires hydroxylation of kynurenine to 3-hydroxykynurenine, but BGC0000296 encodes no such enzyme — unlike sibiromycin (sibC, ACN39726.1, #167) The 3-hydroxyl of 4-MHA requires hydroxylation of kynurenine to 3-hydroxykynurenine, but BGC0000296 encodes no such enzyme. The step is presumably supplied by host primary metabolism (the kynurenine/NAD⁺ pathway)

Three tandem ORFs form and incorporate the C5N ring (PMID 20394362): ALA synthase (ORF34/asuD2) condenses succinyl-CoA + glycine to 5-aminolevulinate, then cyclises ALA-CoA to C5N; acyl-CoA ligase (ORF35/asuD3) makes ALA-CoA via ALA-AMP. The amide synthetase (ORF33 = AAX98208.1 / asuD1 = ADI58645.1) is excluded as the exit reaction — it condenses finished C5N onto the polyenoic acid scaffold.

subclusters.notes: two-protein heme peroxidase that oxidises L-tyrosine to L-DOPA (= 3-hydroxytyrosine). PMID 33373180 provides biochemical evidence that L-DOPA is the precursor of the Dmaq moiety (1,1-dimethyl-3-amino-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-7,8-dihydroxy-quinoline) that caps fabrubactin, and hypothesises the same peroxidase is bifunctional, also catalysing the aza-annulation to Dmaq
